title: How Nike Really Makes Money (The $46 Billion Machine)
description:
Nike sold $46.4 billion of shoes, clothing and gear in fiscal 2026 — yet it owns almost none of the factories that make them. In this file we open the money machine behind Nike: a 1964 handshake and a car full of imported running shoes, the $35 Swoosh and the waffle-iron sole, the Michael Jordan bet and "Just Do It", the 95 contract factories, where the revenue really comes from, the direct-to-consumer bet that backfired, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: NIKE, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 (SEC); NIKE, Inc. fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year results release; NIKE, Inc. fiscal 2027 first-quarter results release; Nike Archives ("The Handshake That Started It All", "Bill Bowerman: Nike's Original Innovator"); Mental Floss; Wikipedia (Nike timeline, Nike, Inc., Just Do It); Boardroom and Hibbett (Air Jordan deal history); Pulse 2.0.

All figures are from company reports where available and are rounded. Gross profit, the footwear share and the Greater China change are our own arithmetic from Nike's reported figures. Early Air Jordan figures are as widely reported, not from Nike's filings. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
